data.title: Arthur Hayes Warns of Weekend Crypto Sell-Off if Fed Does Not Turn Dovish
data.description: Arthur Hayes said cryptocurrencies and other liquid assets could face a sell-off before U.S. stock markets open Monday if the Federal Reserve does not make dovish remarks before close of business Friday (U.S. Eastern Time), ahead of the FOMC quiet period. According to PANews, Hayes said the weekend market could become “exciting” and urged investors to stay safe.

data.title: Sui-Based Bluefin to Shut Down Perpetuals on December 4, 2026
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, Sui-based decentralized exchange Bluefin will stop offering Bluefin Perps perpetual contracts at 21:00 UTC on December 4, 2026. Users must close open positions before trading ends, though withdrawals will remain available for a period afterward.

Bluefin said it has recorded more than $100 billion in cumulative trading volume and has over 2.5 million accounts. Bluefin Perps accounts for 95% of the Sui network’s historical perpetual contract trading volume.

Bluefin said it will focus resources on developing Bluefin Spot and expanding into asset tokenization and real-world assets. The underlying infrastructure for Bluefin Perps will continue to be made available to the community and potential partners through the Bluefin Liquidity Network program.

data.title: Unique Network to Shut Down on January 26, 2027
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, the Polkadot and Kusama ecosystem NFT chain Unique Network will shut down on January 26, 2027, after seven years of operation. The team said it had developed NFT technology but had not attracted users, and that it no longer had enough funding to keep the chain running.

The team recommended that projects built on Unique Network move their collections and NFT issuance to Polkadot AssetHub, with instructions available in Polkadot documentation. Unique Network’s code is open source and available on GitHub for those who need it.

data.title: Fluid Pauses DEX Swaps for Mythos 5.2 Security Review
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, DeFi lending protocol Fluid has paused DEX swaps while it conducts a security review code-named Mythos 5.2.

The protocol said borrowers can continue repaying loans and users can still withdraw funds during the pause. It did not provide a date for when DEX trading will resume.

data.title: Researcher Demonstrates Bitcoin Core Wallet Privacy Vulnerability
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing a post on X, a researcher demonstrated a privacy vulnerability in the Bitcoin Core wallet. In a controlled simulation, the flaw linked Bitcoin addresses to their associated nodes with 100% accuracy. The result was presented as the researcher’s demonstration and has not been independently verified.

data.title: Binance Completes Withdrawal Recovery and Lifts Suspension
data.description:
According to the announcement from Binance, the exchange has completed its withdrawal recovery work and fully lifted the suspension imposed after the October security incident.

Withdrawals remain temporarily paused on a small number of networks undergoing maintenance or planned upgrades. These pauses affect a very small percentage of regular traffic and are separate from the completed recovery work. Binance said it routinely pauses withdrawals on a network when external conditions require it.

For more information, please refer to Binance's official announcements.

data.title: Robin Brooks Warns Hawkish Fed Could Trigger December Crypto and Risk-Asset Meltdown
data.description:
Crypto and other risk assets could face a “full meltdown” before the Federal Reserve’s December rate decision if policymakers maintain a hawkish outlook. According to Cointelegraph, economist Robin Brooks, a senior fellow at the Brookings Institution and former chief foreign exchange strategist at Goldman Sachs, said Wednesday that market turmoil could lead the Fed to abandon the widely expected 25-basis-point rate hike in December. The Fed has continued to signal that rates may need to rise and remain elevated despite falling oil prices and a stronger US dollar. Last week, Federal Reserve Gov. Christopher Waller said policymakers might need to “shock” markets with a 50-basis-point hike to curb businesses passing price increases on to consumers. US WTI crude fell below $80 per barrel for the first time since Aug. 10 this week, reaching $79.25 per barrel, its lowest level since Aug. 10. Brooks called tightening policy as oil prices fall an “error,” arguing it was driving real interest rates higher and adding acute pressure on stocks and other risk assets. He also said the rising dollar was intensifying pressure on emerging markets as a carry trade unwound.

Brooks said risk-asset selling could intensify if the Fed does not act to calm markets before its blackout period. On Nov. 28, the Fed’s blackout period begins ahead of the Dec. 8-9 Federal Open Market Committee meeting, when participants cannot publicly discuss monetary policy or macroeconomic developments. Brooks said the resulting market stress could lead to no rate hike on December 9. The US Dollar Index, which tracks the dollar against a basket of major currencies, reached 104.5 on Monday, its highest level since March, and has remained above 100 since mid-September. US stocks also faced mounting selling pressure: the S&P 500 fell to 6,882 points on Friday, a level last seen in mid-April. Brooks said Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s reinstatement did not lift investor sentiment, while gold recorded its worst 60-day sell-off in over 40 years. Still, CME FedWatch data showed that markets overwhelmingly expected a 25-basis-point increase in December. As of Thursday, the probability of the Fed holding its target rate at 3.75% to 4% was just 0.5%.

data.title: Cryptio Attack Prompts Request for Customers to Revoke API Keys
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, crypto accounting company Cryptio has asked customers to revoke their API keys following an attack, saying credentials used on exchanges and custody platforms may have been exposed.

Cryptio did not confirm that any keys had been stolen and reported no loss of funds. The credentials connect customers’ exchange and custody accounts, and the notice was sent to customers who use Cryptio’s services.

data.title: JPMorgan: Strategy’s Bitcoin Holdings Premium Hits Record Low
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing JPMorgan, the value of Strategy shares relative to its Bitcoin holdings fell to about 0.88 times in a report published Wednesday, below the previous low at the end of June and a record low. The analyst team, led by Nikolaos Panigirtzoglou, compared Strategy’s enterprise value with the dollar value of its Bitcoin holdings. The analysts said the record-low 0.88 net asset value premium for MicroStrategy stock signaled Bitcoin “capitulation.”

Strategy calculates the ratio using its mNAV metric, which divides its share price by the dollar value of net Bitcoin holdings per share and accounts for debt, preferred claims and dollar assets. The company’s website showed an mNAV of 0.88 at 10:39 a.m. U.S. Eastern Time on November 25, before it rose to 0.94.

Bitcoin fell back to about $60,000 after a brief rebound from last week’s low. BlackRock’s IBIT, the largest spot Bitcoin ETF by market capitalization, continued to see net outflows during the brief price rebound, at a faster pace than from early May to the end of June, the analysts said. Last week, they said retail investors may have been the main force behind recent crypto ETF outflows, with some funds possibly moving into stock ETFs. Bitcoin’s price decline also widened the gap between its market price and the estimated production cost of about $86,000, potentially increasing pressure on high-cost miners to sell their Bitcoin reserves.

data.title: Russia's Central Bank Approves Crypto Investor Tests Required Before Purchases
data.description:
Russia's central bank has approved the first standards and rules for testing cryptocurrency investors. According to Foresight News, citing TASS, qualified and non-qualified investors must pass a test before buying cryptocurrency through Russian brokers or crypto exchanges.

The free test consists of eight questions on different topics, and investors must answer at least seven correctly. Topics include market regulation, cryptocurrency characteristics, information security, the risk of transactions being frozen and price volatility. Those who fail may retake the test the same day, with different questions; market participants may not disclose the correct answers.

Passing results are valid for one year, starting from the later of the knowledge assessment date or the last transaction date. Non-qualified investors may invest only in specified types of cryptocurrency and are subject to an annual limit of 300,000 rubles through a single intermediary.

data.title: Injective Urges SEC to Extend Tokenized Stock Trading Exemption Framework to On-Chain Order Books
data.description:
Injective submitted a 22-page policy letter to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), recommending that exemptions for tokenized stock trading be extended to on-chain order books. According to Foresight News, the existing framework covers only some trading venues based on automated market maker (AMM) liquidity pools and does not include order-book models.

Injective called for technology-neutral regulation and proposed investor protections including market surveillance, price limits, measures to prevent self-trading, and protocol-level trading pauses. It also proposed frequent batch auctions to reduce front-running and maximal extractable value (MEV) risks.

This is Injective’s third formal policy submission to the SEC; its previous proposals addressed DeFi protocols and on-chain lending.

data.title: Tom Lee Says U.S. Stocks May Have Bottomed, Rebound Could Precede Fed Policy Shift
data.description:
Bitmine Chairman Tom Lee said U.S. stocks may have reached a market bottom after an extremely painful period, as rising market fear could indicate a low has formed.

According to Odaily, investors staged a broad “buy strike” last week, declining to buy stocks regardless of the news, while the VIX briefly reached 40.

Lee compared current conditions with 2018, when U.S. stocks bottomed on December 24 and the VIX reached 36. The Federal Reserve did not signal a policy shift until January 4 the following year, by which time stocks had rebounded nearly 8%. Lee said stocks could rally before receiving monetary-policy support.
